extracted.intended_audience: medical journal reviewers and editors (biomedical peer reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Operational criteria for assessing the originality and prior dissemination status of submitted manuscripts to medical journals, based on the Ingelfinger Rule and its modern codifications (including handling of preprints and exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingelfinger Rule (verbatim)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Articles are accepted for consideration with the understanding that they are contributed for publication solely in this journal." The journal will not publish findings that have: already been published elsewhere in substantive form, OR been promised to another journal, OR been disseminated in popular media before peer-reviewed publication (with defined exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the foundational originality standard adopted by most major medical journals; it defines the default prohibition on prior/subsequent publication or dissemination except where specific exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: Check for substantive overlap with the authors' own prior publications — does the manuscript present materially the same data or analysis already published?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should identify and cite overlapping prior work; if overlap exists, assess whether the new manuscript provides a materially new contribution rather than merely repeating previously reported data/analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salami slicing
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the dataset has been split into multiple thin publications (salami slicing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag instances where an incremental division of dataset/material produces low-value, fragmented publications; consider whether combined reporting would be more appropriate and whether the incremental contribution justifies a new paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the manuscript been submitted or published simultaneously elsewhere (duplicate submission/publication)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If duplicate submission or prior substantive publication is suspected, notify the editor with specific citation information rather than proceeding with a full substantive review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication media disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the findings been disseminated in popular media before peer-reviewed publication in a way that compromises the journal's consideration?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether media disclosure undermines the journal's claim to novelty; some media/press activity may be acceptable under exceptions (see exceptions), but substantive press dissemination can conflict with the Ingelfinger Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference proceedings / abstracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Does prior conference dissemination cross the threshold of 'substantive prior publication'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most journals permit conference abstracts and short presentations but consider full conference papers or proceedings that contain substantive data/analyses to be prior publication. Treat abstracts as expected and usually not disqualifying unless they contain full methods/results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the manuscript a translation of a paper already published in another language?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations of previously published full papers are typically considered duplicate publication unless explicitly handled/declared and acceptable under journal policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognised exception — public-health emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings that should be communicated immediately for patient safety (e.g., emerging epidemic data) may be exempted from the usual prohibition on prior dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In public-health emergencies, priority of rapid communication can override the Ingelfinger restriction; reviewers/editors should permit rapid disclosure when patient safety demands it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognised exception — regulatory or court-required disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures required by regulators or courts are recognised exceptions to the rule against prior dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disclosure was legally mandated, editors may accept the manuscript despite prior public disclosure; reviewers should note such context and not equate it with improper prior publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognised exception — sponsor press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases by sponsors preceding publication where authors had no control are recognised exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When sponsor-issued communications have released findings without author control, journals may still consider the submission; reviewers should be cautious about penalising authors for sponsor actions beyond their control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognised exception — preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Most journals (since ~2017) accept preprinted submissions; the Ingelfinger Rule has been narrowed to refer to peer-reviewed publication only in many modern codifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not automatically treat preprint posting as disqualifying; check journal policy and, if preprints are accepted, proceed to substantive review without penalising authors for prior preprint posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer norm — flag suspected duplicate to editor
rubrics_metrics.description: If duplicate or prior publication is suspected, reviewers should flag the issue to the editor with specific citation rather than proceeding to substantive review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise bibliographic details/evidence when notifying editors so the editorial office can investigate; avoid spending reviewer effort on manuscripts that may be administratively excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer norm — do not penalise accepted preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not penalise the manuscript merely for prior preprint posting if the journal's policy permits preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the journal's stance on preprints; if allowed, evaluate originality based on novelty relative to peer-reviewed literature, not preprint servers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer norm — treat conference abstracts as expected
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat conference abstract prior publication as expected, not as duplicate publication, unless the conference proceedings include a full paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only consider conference materials as prior publication when they contain substantive methods/results equivalent to a full paper; brief abstracts/posters are generally acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer norm — evaluate incremental contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Where overlap exists with the authors' prior work, reviewers should evaluate whether the incremental contribution is sufficient for a new publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the magnitude and significance of the new analysis/data compared with prior publications; marginal or trivial increments may not justify a separate article under originality standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance for rubric design — 'Originality' criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ingelfinger Rule is the historical anchor for the 'originality' question on medical-journal review forms ('Is the work original? Has it been published or submitted elsewhere?').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modern review rubrics should operationalise originality to include checks for prior publication, simultaneous submission, salami slicing, translations, conference/full-proceedings status, and the journal's preprint policy; include explicit instructions for handling recognised exceptions.
